title: The Real Cost of Chinese Open-Source AI
content:
Don’t believe the Chinese AI open-source hype, warns good friend, Pete Warden. Their large language models come at a price — the models are programmed to deliberately obscure historical truths, he writes on his blog. He points out that this isn’t just censorship; it’s engineered misinformation at scale, baked into the foundation of future AI. Warden compares answers to the same query using different models to support his conclusions.

Chinese companies like Alibaba and DeepSeek are leading the world in open-weights large language and reasoning models. That means these models are likely to become the foundations for thousands of applications worldwide. Any biases in them will propagate through all of those products, and will even be replicated in web pages that are ingested while training future models. The Chinese government’s information control will now have effects worldwide, and they will persist for a long time.

All information retrieval systems, going back to analog libraries and forward to search engines, have biases. What’s different here is that lies are being baked into foundational technologies, with no other perspectives available. YouTube may be driving extremism, but you’ll find a range of views for almost any search. Almost all models have subjects they’ll block queries on, but providing false information by design is something new. It’s bad enough that all LLMs lie accidentally, but models that lie deliberately are even more dangerous.

Pete’s assessment suggests that Chinese authorities have shifted their focus from simply blocking information to creating sophisticated models that provide alternative narratives. You can’t filter these models, for they have finessed and developed evasion techniques and thus will be offering alternative sanitized versions of history that align with government narratives. This represents a fundamental shift from previous censorship approaches.

This is very different from the debates we had around search engines and their neutrality at the turn of the century. Back then, we were rightfully worried about commercial interests influencing search results. Now, we’re facing AI systems that can convincingly rewrite history on a large scale.

This is exactly what I wrote about back in December 2024. “With so many devices becoming part of our daily lives and AI integrating into these devices, we’re likely to see the blurring between neutral technology and tools of influence,” is what I wrote earlier. “It’s increasingly difficult to determine whether AI is offering balanced, factual information or if it is some sort of government-mandated censorship or bias.”

Good to see practitioners of AI engineering are starting to recognize the hidden (and obvious) problems with AI. The lack of viable business models for open-source AI development in Western markets compounds this problem. Where are open-source models from the Western world that are as prevalent as the various models from China?

China views AI as a strategic weapon to control hearts and minds for the next 100 years. It is the ultimate propaganda machine in their world. In the West, where large language models originated, AI is a tool for valuation games.

Pete Warden: Why the Chinese Government Taught AI to Lie
